breadcrumb.name: AC Bill Calculator Pakistan: What an AC Adds to Your Bill

sections.h2: How much will an AC increase my electricity bill?
p: Take the bill without the AC and the bill with it, and subtract. With the defaults, a Split AC 1.5 ton inverter running 8 hours a day adds 240 units to a home that used 180. The bill goes from Rs 3,622 to Rs 21,752, which is Rs 18,130 more a month, or Rs 75.54 for each unit the AC uses.

That is far above the Rs 38.95 slab rate, because the AC does not only add its own units: it re-prices the units the home was already using. Most AC bill calculators multiply the AC's units by one rate and miss this, so their figure is too low exactly when it matters.

sections.h2: Why the AC pushes you into a higher slab
p: On the unprotected domestic tariff every unit is charged at the rate of the slab the monthly total reaches. An unprotected home on 250 units pays Rs 33.10 per unit; with the AC it reaches 490 units and pays Rs 38.95 on all of them. The bill rises by Rs 13,995, Rs 58.31 for each AC unit.
The fixed charge per sanctioned kW also rises with the slab, and the per-unit surcharges and GST grow with the units, so the calculator prices the whole bill twice rather than adding one line.

sections.h2: Protected consumers: the six-month cost of one hot month
p: A home is protected only while each of its last 6 bills stayed within 200 units. A single AC month above that limit moves the home to unprotected rates, and it stays there for the next 6 bills even after the AC is switched off.

With the defaults the penalty on those later bills is Rs 3,669 a month, Rs 22,012 in all, on top of the Rs 18,130 extra in the AC month itself. It is a floor: summer bills with the AC running cost more. If your usage sits just under the limit, fewer AC hours can keep protection, as the third worked example shows.

sections.h2: How to bring the AC's cost down
p: Fewer units in the peak months is what counts: a higher set point, closed doors and curtains, and switching off when the room is empty. An inverter AC uses fewer units than a non-inverter AC of the same tonnage; the inverter AC payback calculator shows how long the price gap takes to recover, and the temperature saving calculator shows what a higher set point saves.

faq.q: How much does a 1.5 ton inverter AC add to the electricity bill?
faq.a: Running 8 hours a day it adds about 240 units a month. For a protected home on 180 units that is Rs 18,130 more a month; for an unprotected home on 250 units, Rs 13,995 more.

faq.q: Why is my bill so high after I started using the AC?
faq.a: Because the AC pushes the whole month into a higher slab or off the protected tariff, and every unit is then charged at the higher rate. In the default example each AC unit really costs Rs 75.54.

faq.q: Will using an AC make me lose protected status?
faq.a: Yes, if the month's total goes over 200 units. Then the next 6 bills are charged at unprotected rates even without the AC; in the default example that costs at least Rs 22,012 more.

faq.q: How many hours can I run an AC and stay protected?
faq.a: Enter your usual units and lower the AC hours until the Protected status lost result shows No. A home on 120 units stays protected with a Split AC 1 ton inverter for 2 hours a day.

faq.q: Is this the same as the AC running cost per month?
faq.a: No. The running cost is the AC's units × one rate. This calculator compares your whole bill with and without the AC, so it includes the slab jump, the fixed charge, surcharges and GST.

faq.q: Does it work for LESCO, IESCO, MEPCO and other DISCOs?
faq.a: Yes. Every DISCO uses the same national domestic tariff; only the FPA and some surcharges differ, and you can enter those from your own bill under Advanced settings.

key_facts: What an AC adds to a Pakistani electricity bill is the bill with the AC minus the bill without it, not the AC's units × one slab rate, because the slab the whole home reaches sets the rate of every unit.
A Split AC 1.5 ton inverter running 8 hours a day for 30 days uses about 240 units a month.
A protected home on 180 units pays about Rs 3,622; adding that AC takes it to 420 units at the unprotected Rs 38.95 rate, about Rs 21,752, so each AC unit really costs Rs 75.54.
One month above 200 units ends protected status: the next 6 bills are charged at unprotected rates even without the AC, at least Rs 22,012 more in this example.
An unprotected home on 250 units pays about Rs 13,995 more a month for the same AC, Rs 58.31 for each AC unit, because the total moves from the Rs 33.10 slab to the Rs 38.95 slab.
mistakes: Multiplying the AC's units by your current slab rate. The AC moves the whole bill to a higher slab, so the real extra is the difference of two full bills.
Forgetting the protected limit. One month over it costs the protected rates for the following bills too, not just that month.
Using a summer bill as the usage without the AC. Take a month when the AC was off, or the AC is counted twice.
Taking the AC's rated input as its average draw. An inverter AC averages well below its label once the room is cool.

how.text: AC: 1 kW × 8 hours = 8 units a day; 8 units × 30 days = 240 units a month. Without the AC: 180 units on the protected tariff = Rs 3,622. With the AC: 420 units on the unprotected tariff at Rs 38.95 per unit = Rs 21,752, including fixed charge, surcharges and GST. Extra: Rs 21,752 − Rs 3,622 = Rs 18,130; Rs 18,130 ÷ 240 AC units = Rs 75.54 for each unit the AC uses. Protection penalty: 6 bills × Rs 3,669 = Rs 22,012.

examples.title: Short evenings with a Split AC 1 ton inverter keep protection
examples.text: 2 hours a day add 39 units, so the home stays at 159 units, within the protected limit. The bill goes from Rs 2,436 to Rs 3,207, only Rs 771 more, and there is no penalty on later bills.

content.answer: A Split AC 1.5 ton inverter running 8 hours a day adds about 240 units a month. For a protected home on 180 units that raises the bill from Rs 3,622 to Rs 21,752, Rs 18,130 more, because every unit moves to the unprotected Rs 38.95 rate. Losing protection then costs at least Rs 22,012 over the next 6 bills.

formula.text: Extra = Bill(other units + AC units) − Bill(other units); AC units = kW_avg × h × days
lines: Bill(units) = energy charge of the slab reached + fixed charge per sanctioned kW + FC surcharge + QTA + FPA, then GST (the electricity bill calculator's method)
kW_avg = the AC's average draw over an hour; h = AC hours a day; days = AC days in the month
A protected home whose total goes over the protected limit is billed at unprotected rates
Penalty = protected months × (Bill of the other units at unprotected rates − Bill of the other units at protected rates)

content.safety: A new AC needs its own circuit with the right cable and MCB, and the home may need a higher sanctioned load. Have a licensed electrician check the wiring before installing it.
